issues.description: Non-cryptographic ID generation using Math.random() and Date.now(). Attackers can predict or enumerate user IDs, leading to unauthorized access or account enumeration.
issues.suggestion: Use cryptographically secure random ID generation: import { randomUUID } from 'crypto'; function generateId(): string { return randomUUID(); }

issues.description: XSS sanitization is incomplete and misapplied. HTML entity encoding is only appropriate for HTML contexts. The email field is not sanitized at all. If data is rendered in JavaScript, URL, or CSS contexts, this encoding is insufficient. Missing encoding for '&' character itself.
issues.suggestion: Remove input sanitization and use context-aware output encoding at render time. For storage, only validate format and length: function sanitizeInput(input: string): string { if (input.length > 500) throw new Error('Input too long'); return input.trim(); }

issues.description: Input validation only checks truthiness, allowing empty strings and whitespace-only values. '!input.email' passes when email is an empty string.
issues.suggestion: Add explicit trim and length validation: if (!input.email?.trim() || !input.name?.trim()) { throw new Error('Email and name are required'); } if (input.name.trim().length < 2 || input.name.length > 100) { throw new Error('Name must be between 2-100 characters'); }

issues.description: Email validation regex /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/ is overly simplistic and allows many invalid email formats. Doesn't prevent all injection vectors or validate against RFC 5322.
issues.suggestion: Use a robust email validation library like 'validator' or a stricter regex. Consider: import validator from 'validator'; export function isValidEmail(email: string): boolean { return validator.isEmail(email); }

issues.description: Missing error handling for database operation. No try/catch to handle constraint violations (duplicate email/ID), connection failures, or other database errors. Unhandled errors could leak schema information.
issues.suggestion: Add proper error handling: async function saveUser(user: User): Promise<void> { try { const query = 'INSERT INTO users (id, email, name, created_at) VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4)'; const params = [user.id, user.email, user.name, user.createdAt]; // await db.query(query, params); } catch (error) { throw new Error('Failed to create user'); } }

issues.description: Function doesn't handle null or undefined input. Will throw runtime error if called with null/undefined instead of returning false.
issues.suggestion: Add null check: export function isValidEmail(email: string | null | undefined): boolean { if (!email) return false; const emailRegex = /^[^\s@]+@[^\s@]+\.[^\s@]+$/; return emailRegex.test(email); }

issues.description: Email field has no length validation or sanitization, only toLowerCase(). Excessively long emails could cause storage issues or DoS.
issues.suggestion: Add length validation before processing: if (input.email.length > 254) { throw new Error('Email too long'); }

issues.description: Function throws generic Error objects. Consumers cannot distinguish between different validation failure types (missing field, invalid format, database error) for proper error handling.
issues.suggestion: Consider custom error types or error result pattern: class ValidationError extends Error { constructor(message: string) { super(message); this.name = 'ValidationError'; } }

issues.description: Four chained replace() calls each iterate through the entire string (O(4n)). Could be optimized to single pass O(n).
issues.suggestion: Use single replace with lookup function: return input.replace(/[<>\"']/g, (char) => ({ '<': '<', '>': '>', '\"': '"', "'": ''' }[char] || char));

issues.description: sanitizeInput doesn't handle null or undefined input, will throw runtime error on method chaining.
issues.suggestion: Add validation: export function sanitizeInput(input: string | null | undefined): string { if (!input) return ''; return input.replace(...); }

codeQuality.summary: This file demonstrates good intentions with input validation and parameterized queries, but has critical security flaws in ID generation (predictable) and XSS prevention (misapplied sanitization). Multiple input validation gaps allow empty/null values through. With 1 critical-equivalent high + 5 medium + 3 low issues: 100 - 15 - (5×7) - (3×3) = 44/100.

testCoverage.summary: No tests exist for this file. All 5 exported functions and multiple critical security paths (XSS prevention, email validation, input sanitization) are completely untested. Estimated 0% coverage.

suggestions.description: Extract input validation logic into a separate validation function to separate concerns and improve testability
suggestions.benefits: Separates validation logic from business logic, making each function easier to test, understand, and reuse. Validation can be tested independently and potentially reused in other contexts.

suggestions.description: Replace chained replace calls with a lookup table pattern for better maintainability and performance
suggestions.benefits: Single regex pass instead of four separate passes improves performance. Lookup table makes it easier to add/remove escape characters and see all mappings at once.

suggestions.description: Use destructuring and computed property names for cleaner object construction
suggestions.benefits: Creates a clear separation between user object construction and the create workflow. Makes the createUser function read more declaratively and easier to test user object creation independently.

suggestions.description: Apply the Builder or Factory pattern with a UserService class to encapsulate related operations and improve dependency injection
suggestions.benefits: Enables dependency injection for testing (mock validator, sanitizer, repository). Groups related user operations together. Makes it easy to swap implementations (e.g., different ID generation strategies, database backends). Follows SOLID principles, particularly Single Responsibility and Dependency Inversion.

suggestions.description: Make email regex a constant at module level for reusability and avoid recompiling the regex on each call
suggestions.benefits: Prevents regex recompilation on every function call, improving performance slightly. Makes the regex pattern easier to reference and test independently. Follows the DRY principle if the pattern needs to be used elsewhere.

suggestions.description: Consider using crypto.randomUUID() for more robust ID generation if available in the target environment
suggestions.benefits: Using crypto.randomUUID() provides better uniqueness guarantees and follows modern standards. If not available, breaking down the concatenation into named variables improves readability and makes the generation strategy explicit.

suggestions.description: Create a proper UserRepository interface/class instead of a loose function to formalize the data access layer
suggestions.benefits: Creates a clear contract for data access operations. Makes it trivial to create mock implementations for testing. Allows different persistence strategies (Postgres, MongoDB, in-memory) to be swapped without changing business logic. Follows the Repository pattern from Domain-Driven Design.

suggestions.description: Consider adding branded types for email to enforce validation at the type level
suggestions.benefits: Enforces email validation at compile time, preventing unvalidated emails from being passed to functions expecting validated ones. This is a type-level guarantee that reduces runtime errors and makes the API self-documenting.

refactorings.summary: The code is already well-structured with good separation of concerns. Main opportunities include extracting validation logic into a dedicated function, applying the Service/Repository pattern for better dependency injection and testability, and using lookup tables for the sanitization logic to improve performance and maintainability.

recommendations.description: Add comprehensive test suite for security-critical functions. The file has 0% test coverage with no tests for XSS prevention (sanitizeInput), email validation, or user creation flow. All validation paths and edge cases are untested, leaving critical security vulnerabilities undetected.

Replace Math.random() ID generation with cryptographically secure crypto.randomUUID(). Current implementation enables account enumeration attacks and ID prediction, allowing unauthorized access to user accounts.

Redesign XSS prevention strategy. Current HTML entity encoding is misapplied for input sanitization and incomplete (missing '&' encoding). Replace with context-aware output encoding at render time and proper input validation (length, format) at storage time.

Strengthen input validation to prevent empty/whitespace-only values. Add explicit .trim() checks, length validation (2-100 chars for names, max 254 for emails), and handle null/undefined inputs gracefully in isValidEmail and sanitizeInput functions.

Improve email validation using a robust library like 'validator' or RFC 5322-compliant regex. Current regex allows many invalid formats and doesn't prevent injection vectors or validate international characters.

Add comprehensive error handling for database operations in saveUser(). Include try-catch blocks for constraint violations, connection failures, and schema errors. Use custom error types to allow consumers to distinguish between validation, database, and other failures.

Extract validation logic into a dedicated validateCreateUserInput() function and apply Service/Repository pattern. This improves testability, enables dependency injection for mocking, and follows SOLID principles for better maintainability.

Optimize sanitizeInput() to use single-pass regex with lookup table instead of four chained replace() calls. This reduces time complexity from O(4n) to O(n) and improves maintainability by centralizing character mappings.
